quotes.text: A case is one record for one customer issue that needs an answer or a fix, and the issue could be a damaged product, a billing question, a login problem, or a request for help using a service.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Plain-English definition of a case with concrete examples.

quotes.text: A queue is a shared work tray for a team. It isn't one agent's inbox and it doesn't belong to the person who first saw the request.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable analogy that clarifies team ownership of work.

quotes.text: An SLA attaches a clock to the case, so the team knows exactly how long they have to meet a customer promise.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains SLAs in one concrete image.

quotes.text: Case management isn't really about filling out a ticket screen. It's about giving every customer issue a clear path or recorded answer and a team that can learn from what happened.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up the purpose of case management beyond ticketing.

chapters.title: From intake to the right queue

takeaways: A case in Dynamics 365 Customer Service is one record per customer issue that keeps details, activities and history together.
Record creation rules, queues and routing rules get each case to the right team, while parent cases and merging handle outages and duplicates.
SLAs track first response and resolution targets separately, and recorded resolutions plus case data help teams learn and reduce future volume.
hook: Customers who repeat their story across email, phone and chat are a sign that support context is getting lost. This episode explains Dynamics 365 Case Management in plain English for service teams and leads. You learn how cases, queues, routing, SLAs, knowledge articles and resolutions keep the whole customer story in one place.
